- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecasted drop magnitude.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days — cap forecast decline to 5–7% below peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a dip, model frequently underreacts — increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when recent prices are volatile — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.50), model tends to forecast flat or slightly downward — adjust upward by 0.3–0.8% to reflect hidden support.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 2–5 days — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to compensate for lag.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >1.5), model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 0.5–1.2% for next 5–7 days.
